rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A moderate temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in subsequent injections.
Change temperature alone to test whether selectivity separates the critical middle cluster. The initial run leaves ample time margin, so resolving the weakest pair is the priority.

Test the upper temperature limit while holding the gradient fixed to map selectivity changes in the middle cluster. This will show whether the improved separation at 50 C continues or another pair becomes limiting.
Use a shallower gradient at the best temperature so far to improve the unresolved middle pair. The 6.49-minute last peak leaves substantial room to gain resolution without incurring a time penalty.

Combine the shallower gradient's improved spacing in the earlier middle pair with a temperature increase intended to separate the later critical pair. This intermediate temperature may balance both selectivity constraints while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.
Injection 5 achieved the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to test whether full resolution can be maintained with faster elution.

Reduce the endpoint to make the 12-minute gradient slightly steeper than the fully resolved benchmark but shallower than injection 6. This should recover the limiting pair's resolution while modestly shortening elution relative to injection 5.

Increase the gradient slope slightly from 0.0625 to 0.065 organic fraction per minute to seek faster elution while preserving full resolution. Injection 7 remains the fastest confirmed method with maximum CRF.

Raise the starting organic fraction while preserving injection 8's gradient slope to test whether the elution window can move earlier without losing full resolution. Retain injection 8 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method if either critical pair deteriorates.

Probe lower-temperature selectivity as an alternative route to a faster fully resolved method, since the 55 C region is constrained by two competing critical pairs. Injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test whether a lower starting organic fraction restores spacing in the earlier critical pair enough to permit a steeper gradient. This explores a potentially faster fully resolved method while retaining injection 8 as the benchmark.

Lengthen injection 11's gradient by one step to improve its limiting pair while testing whether the later critical pair remains resolved. This may achieve maximum CRF with earlier final elution than injection 8.

Test a substantially steeper gradient at 60 C to see whether the previously crossing middle pair separates on the opposite side of its selectivity crossover. This explores a much faster alternative while retaining injection 12 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test higher starting organic at 60 C to shift the middle-pair selectivity beyond its crossover without the severe compression of the six-minute gradient. Injection 12 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Test whether a shallower gradient at 40 C resolves the middle cluster in its alternative elution order. The expected last-peak time remains below 10 minutes, and injection 12 is retained as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test whether lowering the starting organic fraction improves the critical middle-pair selectivity at 40 C enough to support a shorter gradient. Compare with injection 12 to isolate temperature effects under this gradient, retaining its maximum-score result as the benchmark.

Test a shallower gradient with the higher starting organic fraction to recover the earlier critical pair while preserving the later pair's improved separation. This targets greater resolution margin at maximum CRF; injection 12 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Lower the endpoint one step to recover injection 17's nearly resolved pair, with the last peak expected to remain below 10 minutes. This seeks a maximum-score alternative with greater resolution margin while retaining injection 12 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Preserve injection 12's successful gradient slope but end the ramp earlier, after its last peak is expected to elute. This should retain maximum CRF while shortening the programmed gradient from 12 to 8 minutes.

Test a small slope increase over injection 8 to locate the full-resolution boundary more precisely. The limiting pair may fall just below 1.5; injections 12 and 19 remain the fastest confirmed maximum-score methods.

Increase the slope slightly from the fastest confirmed fully resolved method to test its resolution boundary. This targets earlier final elution while retaining injections 12 and 19 as maximum-score benchmarks.

Test whether a steeper gradient and higher starting organic fraction improve the later critical pair at 50 C while its earlier pair remains resolved. This targets a faster alternative; injection 19 remains the preferred confirmed maximum-score method.

Preserve injection 19's resolving slope but enter the final hold earlier, after the critical cluster has eluted. Test whether the last compound still elutes within 10 minutes, allowing a shorter programmed gradient without sacrificing maximum CRF.

Use a slightly shallower gradient than injection 7 to seek a better balance between the two critical pairs while keeping final elution below 10 minutes. Injection 19 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method; this run targets additional resolution margin.

Preserve injection 7's fully resolving slope while ending the gradient earlier, with the outlet ramp still extending beyond its 8.00-minute last peak. This should retain maximum CRF in a shorter programmed gradient; injection 19 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.
